content.headline: No women on the stage
content.body: In Shakespeare's lifetime every female role, Juliet included, was played by a boy. Women first acted on England's public stage in the 1660s.

content.headline: The Rose
content.body: Henslowe's Rose, built in 1587, was Bankside's first playhouse. Its foundations were rediscovered in 1989.

content.headline: An old story
content.body: Romeo and Juliet was already an old tale. Shakespeare took it from Arthur Brooke's poem of 1562.

content.headline: Order your interval drinks now
content.body: Tell the bar what you'd like before curtain up, and it will be poured and waiting for you.
content.footline: Order at the bar, or ask front-of-house
